releases.body:
### Patch Changes

- eb346c9: Policy 22 now judges every interactive-command pattern at command position, matching how monitors and pagers already worked. An editor name, `sudo`, `git rebase -i`, `git add -p`, or an unconfirmed `npm init` / apt / yum install that appears only as an argument is data, so `grep -n 'sudo'`, `grep -n 'git rebase -i'`, and `printf "%s" "vim is not installed"` are allowed. The commands themselves still block, including behind wrappers (`env FOO=1 sudo ls`, `timeout 5 sudo ls`), in a control-flow body (`while true; do sudo ls; done`, `then apt-get install curl`), through `eval`, through `sh -c`, and via `busybox`. A `sudo` wrapper is reported by the shell unwrapper, because unwrapping removes it before the command word. A command name delivered to a shell as stdin data (`echo 'vim x' | sh`) is a documented limitation.
- 1d3ff3d: Policy 6 no longer treats a copy source under a config path as a settings mutation when no live control plane is declared. `cp`, `ln -s`, and `install` are judged by their destination operand, so `cp ~/.config/opencode/templates/x ./draft.md` is allowed. A guarded destination still blocks, including through `-t`, `--target-directory=`, and `install -d`. A hard link stays blocked because it is a second writable name for the guarded inode, so `ln` without `-s` and `cp -l`/`--link` keep the broad match. `mv` keeps the broad any-operand match because the move removes its source. A guarded destination written after an fd duplication (`2>&1`) is now blocked as well; the duplication no longer splits the command into a fragment the guard does not read.

### Patch Changes

- f465f87: Allow a stale protected checkout to sync. `git merge --ff-only [<ref>]`, `git rebase <ref>`, and `git pull --ff-only` are now permitted on `main`/`master` when the target is the branch's tracked upstream or the remote default and `HEAD` is already an ancestor of it, so the sync adds no commit and rewrites none.

    A protected branch with no safe sync path was the defect: every remote refresh was refused with "create a feature branch first", which left the primary checkout permanently stale. The exemption stays narrow. `git merge` without `--ff-only`, a bare `git pull`, a local branch target, a different remote branch, a named remote and branch, and a diverged branch all stay blocked.

    An unqualified `git pull` on a protected branch is now a blocked history write rather than an unclassified command, because with `pull.rebase` set it replays local commits. The permission seat defers any `pull` to `execute.before`, since whether the checkout is protected is a fact the seat cannot see.

### Minor Changes

- 4e63e6d: Refuse shell-spawned agent CLIs, and close the live-system and self-config gaps around them.

    - New Policy 28 blocks `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `aider`, and `opencode run` in command position. It unwraps shell wrappers, chained segments, `npx`/`bunx` package execution, and inline interpreter payloads first, so a spawned agent cannot bypass the guard's hooks. The host's `task` tool remains the governed path to a subagent.
    - Policy 4 now blocks Azure RBAC role-assignment changes, PR merges through `gh`, and raw DELETE requests through `gh api`, including wrapped and chained forms.
    - Policy 6 now blocks the `opencode plugin` and `opencode mcp` mutating verbs, so an agent cannot remove or replace the guard from its own control plane. Read-only listing stays allowed.

### Patch Changes

- 2b045c5: `guard_review_rubric` now names the workspace, base ref, and diff byte count it graded in a `Provenance:` line. When no listed base yields a diff it refuses with the workspace, every base it tried, and the remedy, instead of silently grading `git diff HEAD~1`. `HEAD~1` is graded only when the caller passes `base: "HEAD~1"`.

    The injected workflow guidance and both tool descriptions now say the calling session records the reviewer subagent's verdict, because a reviewer agent's host permission list may omit `record_review`.

    A recognized shell writer (redirect, `tee`, `sed -i`, `cp`/`mv`/`ln`, `rm`, `truncate`, `dd of=`, `git apply`, `git am`, and a `mv` source) is now refused when its target is claimed by another session, matching the direct-edit claim check. A shell write never acquires a claim, so it cannot strand one.

### Patch Changes

- aacd45a: Expose the provenance of verification and review evidence in `guard_status`.

    - `guard_status.lastVerify` now reports its observation timestamp and duration beside the command, pass state, freshness, evidence id, and commit hash. A configured `verifyCommand` that runs green therefore leaves a record naming when it ran and the commit it covered, instead of only an anonymous evidence id.
    - `guard_status.lastReview` now reports its observation timestamp together with `recorderSessionID`, `recorderRole` (`root` or `subagent`), and `targetSessionID`. Under `requireSubagentReview`, this shows that an approval came from a subagent session rather than the root session it was recorded for.
    - `record_review` keeps the recorder lineage on the stored verdict, and the durable review cache carries the same optional fields. `record_review` itself stays registered for every session; a deny-all reviewer toolset still needs the host permission grant in its own agent definition.
